content: The revised Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) emphasizes the protection, promotion, and support of breastfeeding in facilities providing maternity and newborn services. Below are key indicators and practices for monitoring the implementation of this initiative: 1. Discussing Breastfeeding with Pregnant Women and Families: At least 80% of mothers of preterm and term infants should report that a staff member informed them about where to access breastfeeding support in their community. This is assessed through interviews with mothers. 2. Training of Health Professionals: At least 80% of health professionals providing antenatal, delivery, or newborn care should report receiving pre-service or in-service breastfeeding training within the past two years. Additionally, at least 80% should report undergoing competency assessments in breastfeeding during the same period. Furthermore, at least 80% of these professionals should be able to correctly answer three out of four questions on breastfeeding knowledge and skills. These indicators are evaluated through interviews with clinical staff. 3. Exclusive Breastfeeding in Infants Under Six Months: The percentage of infants aged 0–5 months who received only breast milk during the previous day is monitored through household surveys such as MICS (Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys) or DHS (Demographic and Health Surveys). 4. Births in Baby-Friendly Facilities: The percentage of births occurring in facilities designated as Baby-Friendly (having passed external assessments or meeting compliance standards within the past five years) is tracked through program implementation reports and national databases. 5. Antenatal Counseling on Breastfeeding: The percentage of mothers who received antenatal counseling on breastfeeding is assessed through household surveys, health management information systems (HMIS), exit interviews, or facility surveys. 6. Early Skin-to-Skin Contact: The percentage of mothers who had skin-to-skin contact with their baby immediately or within five minutes after birth, lasting at least one hour, is monitored through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 7. Early Initiation of Breastfeeding: The percentage of mothers who put their infant to the breast within one hour after birth is evaluated using household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 8. Support with Breastfeeding: The percentage of mothers who received support in learning to breastfeed after delivery is assessed through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 9. Exclusive Breastfeeding During Facility Stay: The percentage of mothers reporting that their infants received only breast milk (from their own mother or a human milk bank) throughout their stay at the facility is monitored through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 10. Rooming-In: The percentage of mothers whose babies stayed with them since birth without separation lasting more than one hour is tracked through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 11. Referral to Community Support: The percentage of mothers who report being informed about where to access breastfeeding support in their community is assessed through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 12. Overall Compliance with BFHI Standards: The percentage of mothers affirming at least six out of seven key breastfeeding practices is monitored through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 13. Regulation of BFHI Standards: The percentage of provinces, states, or districts with regulations on Baby-Friendly standards is tracked through country-level reports. 14. Pre-Service Training on BFHI Standards: The percentage of newly graduated health professionals who received training on updated BFHI standards is monitored through country-level reports. 15. In-Service Training on BFHI Standards: The percentage of practicing health professionals who received in-service training on updated BFHI standards is assessed through country-level reports. 16. External Assessment of Facilities: The percentage of facilities providing maternity and newborn services that have completed an external assessment in the past 3–5 years is tracked through country-level reports. These indicators are critical for ensuring the successful implementation of the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative and improving breastfeeding practices globally.
